caption.en: 🗻 EST II Mathematics Level 2 — Content Areas

rows.en: Complex numbers, sequences & series, advanced equations
Limits, an introduction to differential equations

body.en: EST II — the individual subject test taken alongside EST I by students applying to practical colleges (Medicine, Engineering, Pharmacy, and similar) — has two separate math components. Math Level 1 covers algebra, geometry, trigonometry, and statistics at the level EST I already builds toward. Math Level 2, covered here, goes further: complex numbers, matrices and vectors, sequences and series, and an introduction to calculus — the material that distinguishes students aiming for the most competitive, math-heavy programs.

body.en: EST II Math Level 2 is a timed, multiple-choice exam; a calculator is permitted, and a formula reference sheet is printed in the test booklet. Because the same booklet formula sheet covers most standard identities, the highest-value study time is spent on applying formulas correctly under time pressure, not re-memorizing ones you'll be handed anyway.

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Level 2 Strategic Approach

body.en:
EST II Math Level 2 questions reward quick conceptual recognition. Key priorities include:

  • Algebraic Checks: Verify roots in original logarithmic and rational expressions to eliminate extraneous answers.
  • Geometric Visuals: Sketch vectors, complex plane points, and function graphs to verify signs and quadrants before calculating.

label.en: ⚠ EST II Timing Pitfalls & Calculator Hazards

body.en:
Pacing Strategy: The test has 50 questions in 60 minutes (72 seconds/question). Do not spend more than 2 minutes on any single question on the first pass; flag it and return.

Calculator Precision: Avoid rounding intermediate values during multi-step matrix or trigonometry problems, which causes final rounding errors that lead to distractor choices.

No Guessing Penalty: EST II does not deduct points for incorrect answers; always ensure every question is answered before time expires.

label.en: Worked Example A — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0 \implies x = 2 \text{ or } x = 3 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 2 + 3 = \mathbf{5} \) and product \( = (2)(3) = \mathbf{6} \).

label.en: Worked Example B — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 3)(x - 6) = 0 \implies x = 3 \text{ or } x = 6 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 3 + 6 = \mathbf{9} \) and product \( = (3)(6) = \mathbf{18} \).

label.en: Worked Example C — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 13x + 36 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 4)(x - 9) = 0 \implies x = 4 \text{ or } x = 9 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 4 + 9 = \mathbf{13} \) and product \( = (4)(9) = \mathbf{36} \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 10x + 25 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 5)(x - 5) = 0 \implies x = 5 \text{ or } x = 5 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 5 + 5 = \mathbf{10} \) and product \( = (5)(5) = \mathbf{25} \).

question.en: A student answers 35 questions in 42 minutes. To finish all 50 questions on the exam, how many seconds per question must the student maintain for the remaining questions?

solution.en: The exam has \(60\text{ minutes} = 3600\text{ seconds}\) total. 42 minutes is \(42 \times 60 = 2520\text{ seconds}\). The remaining time is \(3600 - 2520 = 1080\text{ seconds}\). The remaining number of questions is \(50 - 35 = 15\). The allowed pacing is \(\dfrac{1080\text{ seconds}}{15\text{ questions}} = 72\text{ seconds per question}\).

question.en: [Test format & strategy · Practice 2] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 4t + 4 \), evaluate \( g(6) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 32 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 6 \): \( g(6) = 4(6) + 4 = \mathbf{28} \). Setting \( 4t + 4 = 32 \) gives \( 4t = 28 \implies t = \mathbf{7} \).

question.en: [Test format & strategy · Practice 3] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 5t + 5 \), evaluate \( g(8) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 50 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 8 \): \( g(8) = 5(8) + 5 = \mathbf{45} \). Setting \( 5t + 5 = 50 \) gives \( 5t = 45 \implies t = \mathbf{9} \).

question.en: [Test format & strategy · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
